sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked for details about the outsourcing arrangement to private sector companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: These amendments do not involve the automation of enforcement decisions.

sections.label: Mobility scooter medical needs assessment
sections.summary: MHA is working with the Sentencing Advisory Panel on driving sentencing guidelines, and mobility scooters are not banned but safeguarded for those with medical needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Building on this, MHA is working with the Sentencing Advisory Panel, chaired by Justice Tay Yong Kwang, to publish sentencing guidelines for the offences of dangerous and careless driving.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: At the outset, I wish to make clear that we are not banning the use of mobility scooters but safeguarding them for those who truly need them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Several Members, like Ms Joan Pereira, Ms Choo Pei Ling and Dr Haresh Singaraju spoke about how medical needs will be assessed to allow for the use of mobility scooters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will need the support of our doctors and occupational therapists (OTs), to assess the medical needs to determine whether a person's medical conditions lead to mobility challenges that require a mobility scooter.

sections.label: Registry of medical need certificates
sections.summary: The Government will maintain a registry of those with valid Certificates of Medical Need and those exempted from the requirement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The Government will maintain a registry of those with valid Certificates of Medical Need and those exempted from the requirement.

sections.label: No subsidies for certificate visits
sections.summary: Healthcare subsidies will not be accorded for visits made solely to obtain the Certificate of Medical Need.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Healthcare subsidies will not be accorded for visits made solely to obtain the Certificate of Medical Need.

sections.label: Delivery riders switching from PMAs
sections.summary: Delivery riders without mobility challenges should switch to other devices or vehicles before 1 June 2026, with industry support for new PMA rules.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: For delivery riders without mobility challenges, PMAs are not the right mode of transport for them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: They can continue their trade by switching to other devices or vehicles before 1 June 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We had engaged the Digital Platforms Industry Association and the NDCA last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: They expressed support for the new PMA rules, including the six kilometres an hour speed limit, in a joint statement.

sections.label: PMA rules transition period
sections.summary: Stakeholders had time to switch before PMA rules start 1 June 2026, but mobility scooter users get until 1 January 2029 to register and comply with the six kilometres per hour speed limit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Affected stakeholders, including retailers and users, have had time to change to compliant devices before the PMA rules commence on 1 June 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: But we will provide more time, until 1 January 2029, for existing mobility scooter users to register their devices and change to devices that comply with the new maximum device speed of six kilometres per hour.

sections.label: PAB registration cost comparison
sections.summary: The current cost of registering PABs is $50.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: As a comparison, the current cost of registering PABs is $50.

sections.label: Mobility scooter registration framework
sections.summary: Registration and identification marks show the device's unique identification number, not owner details; generally only Certificate of Medical Need holders or exempted individuals can register mobility scooters, and families can share one.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Registration and identification marks will display the device's unique identification number rather than personal details of the owner, similar to e-scooters, where it is a sticker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In addition, as a general rule, only individuals granted a Certificate of Medical Need or exempted from the requirement can register mobility scooters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The registration framework will allow families to share a single mobility scooter.

sections.label: Prosecution for keeping unsafe device
sections.summary: The individual can also be prosecuted for the offence of keeping the unsafe device.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The individual can also be prosecuted for the offence of keeping the unsafe device.

sections.label: E-scooter periodic inspections
sections.summary: Periodic inspections are required for e-scooters to check they remain compliant with the UL2272 standard and have not been illegally modified.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Today, periodic inspections are required for e-scooters to check that they remain compliant with the UL2272 standard and have not been illegally modified.

sections.label: Online sales enforcement and rules
sections.summary: LTA works with e-commerce platforms Carousell, Lazada and Shopee to take down non-compliant device listings, and will look at strengthening rules for online sales and advertising in legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: LTA actively works with major e-commerce platforms like Carousell, Lazada and Shopee to take down listings of non-compliant devices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will look at how we can strengthen rules for online sales and advertising in our legislation.

sections.label: Certificate of Medical Need
sections.summary: The Certificate of Medical Need distinguishes genuine users from those who misuse mobility scooters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: With the Certificate of Medical Need, we distinguish genuine users from those who misuse mobility scooters.

sections.label: ERP payment penalties
sections.summary: This amendment makes penalties more proportionate to the offence, as most missed ERP payments are due to genuine oversight.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Indeed, most missed ERP payments are due to genuine oversight rather than an intent to avoid payment.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: This amendment would therefore make the penalties more proportionate to the offence.

sections.label: LTA vehicle-specific data use
sections.summary: LTA will use vehicle-specific data only for payment, charges and enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: As we have said before, LTA will use vehicle-specific data only for payment, charges and enforcement.

sections.label: OBU exemption for old cars
sections.summary: Old cars on the Classic or Vintage Vehicle schemes will be exempt from installing an OBU where technical problems cannot be resolved.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Where technical problems cannot be resolved such as old cars on the Classic or Vintage Vehicle schemes, we will exempt them from the requirement to install an OBU.

sections.label: Sitting suspension
sections.summary: The Sitting is suspended and the Chair will be taken at 5.05 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Clarification for the Minister, the Senior Minister of State and the Minister of State?

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Looks like the round-up speeches by the three officeholders are very comprehensive.      .

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 5.05 pm.
